record.tranche_reason: Tests whether changing the activation function affects the depth and convergence of plain networks, using feedforward MLPs and convergence/accuracy outcomes rather than the claim version’s convolutional training-error comparison.
record.gate_note: The study reports convergence and test-time accuracy, not training classification error. Its eigenvalue-spectrum discussion bears on network geometry but does not measure a version’s stated training-error outcome. Referenced results from other studies are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses initialization and signal-propagation theory to design an activation function and evaluates that intervention. It holds orthogonal initialization fixed, so it does not test V4's initialization effects. Its unnormalized MLP convergence and test-accuracy results do not test V3's training-error degradation in batch-normalized convolutional networks or its identity-shortcut comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the conclusion: static normalization of ReLU enables deeper MLP training and improves convergence speed and robustness. These are activation-intervention findings under default orthogonal initialization, not evidence comparing initialization schemes or residual shortcuts.
record.recipe_differences: Applies a static Hermite-based normalization to ReLU and trains orthogonally initialized feedforward MLPs on CIFAR10; it does not test the residual shortcut intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: Activation choice and width affect the reported convergence and accuracy outcomes; the text says tilting is less efficient at width 128 than at width 1024.

fits_no_version.finding: With orthogonal initialization held fixed, tilted ReLU permits convergence through 60 MLP layers, while standard ReLU stops converging beyond approximately 30.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation choice affects the trainable depth of plain, unnormalized CIFAR-10 MLPs.

fits_no_version.finding: At 30 layers and width 1024, tilted ReLU reaches test accuracy comparable to tanh after about 25 epochs, while standard ReLU struggles to converge.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Static ReLU normalization improves convergence and test-accuracy progress under fixed orthogonal initialization.

fits_no_version.finding: At width 128, removing centering preserves convergence and performs at least as well; tilted activations have weaker terminal accuracy than at greater width, whereas ELU avoids this reported deterioration.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The benefits of tilted activations depend on width, and centering is unnecessary for their convergence benefit in this setup.

record.problems: Results are qualitative in the supplied text and several outcomes are described by reference to figures without numerical values. The measured accuracy is test-time accuracy, not training classification error; no control or uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: The study discusses eigenvalue spectra and batch-normalization effects in Section 5.3, including figure-based descriptions, but these do not measure a version’s stated training-error outcome. Cited prior work is excluded.

untested.parts: Training classification error in convolutional networks, including random labels, model-size effects, and training-recipe qualifications.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious local minima, and excess student width.
Depth-related training-error degradation in batch-normalized convolutional networks, identity-shortcut comparisons, and the specified tanh and Fixup exceptions.
Effects of changing initialization on training speed and trainable depth, activation-matched initialization comparisons, Gaussian versus orthogonal weights, and very deep convolutional kernels.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss and curvature dynamics, recovery, and divergence.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons. The reported spectral change with batch normalization does not measure these outcomes.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text contains qualitative convergence statements and figure captions, but no readable numerical accuracy curves. Missing training-error measurements and initialization controls are untested outcomes, not scope-limiting results.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, random or corrupted labels, CIFAR-100, model size effects on that measure, and early stopping or regularized recipes.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Batch-normalized convolutional networks, identity shortcut comparisons, training error values, ImageNet, CIFAR-10 residual networks, and Fixup or deep tanh results.
Comparisons among initialization schemes, activation-matched initialization, tanh networks, Gaussian versus orthogonal weights, and very deep convolutional networks.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss spikes, curvature or sharpness dynamics, and divergence.
Batch normalization comparisons, higher learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup-trained residual networks.

rows.subject: feedforward network with tilted ReLU
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR10 while progressively increasing network depth; no batch normalization.
rows.value: Provides convergence all the way to 60 layers.
rows.note: The paper reports convergence, not training classification error.
rows.check: Convergence through 60 layers evaluates the proposed activation in an MLP without batch normalization; it does not measure V3's training-error comparison. Width 1024 is not explicitly assigned to this depth sweep in Section 5.2.1.

rows.subject: feedforward network with ReLU
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR10 while progressively increasing network depth; no batch normalization.
rows.value: Stops converging after depth reaches circa 30 layers.
rows.note: The comparison is to the tilted ReLU setup; the text describes convergence, not training error.
rows.check: Failure to converge beyond approximately 30 layers concerns an unnormalized ReLU MLP, not V3's batch-normalized convolutional networks. Width 1024 is not explicitly assigned to this depth sweep.

rows.subject: 30-layer feedforward network with tilted ReLU
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR10; test-time accuracy plotted over training epochs.
rows.value: Accuracy and convergence speed are in line with the hyperbolic tangent unit; reaches this after about 25 epochs.
rows.note: No numerical accuracy value is stated in the text; this is test-time accuracy, not training error.
rows.check: Figure 4 compares activation functions using test accuracy over epochs at fixed depth and initialization. It measures neither training-error degradation nor an initialization intervention.

rows.subject: 30-layer feedforward network with ReLU
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR10; compared in test-time accuracy over training epochs.
rows.value: Barely converges; across many runs it shows difficulty converging.
rows.note: Qualitative result; the text gives no numerical accuracy.
rows.check: The qualitative convergence difficulty is an activation comparator at fixed MLP depth; it does not establish any version's effect.

rows.subject: feedforward network with noncentered tilted ReLU
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR10 and compared with the centered tilted unit.
rows.value: Performs as well, actually better, as the centered unit and maintains convergence.
rows.note: The paper says reduced width makes tilting less efficient as judged by terminal accuracy, but gives no numerical accuracy values in the text.
rows.check: This compares centering choices for the proposed activation using convergence and test accuracy, outside the versions.

rows.subject: feedforward network with centered tilted ReLU
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR10; compared with the noncentered tilted unit.
rows.value: The noncentered tilted unit performs as well, actually better.
rows.note: Comparison stated qualitatively; no numerical accuracy values are supplied in the text.
rows.check: This repeats R5's centered-versus-noncentered comparison from the comparator's perspective rather than recording an independent result.

rows.subject: feedforward network with ELU
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR10; compared with tilted activations.
rows.value: The ELU unit does not suffer the reduced terminal-accuracy efficiency described for tilting at the decreased width.
rows.note: Qualitative comparison to the stated width effect; the paper gives no numerical values.
rows.check: The ELU terminal-test-accuracy comparison concerns activation performance at reduced width, outside the versions.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: plain CIFAR10 feedforward MLPs without batch normalization
reader_labels.reason: Changing the activation is associated with convergence to 60 layers while ReLU stops around 30, so the observed depth limit depends on activation; R1–R2. The 30-layer accuracy comparisons are also qualitative and do not report training error; R3–R7.
